drafter.private_reasoning: I revised the first draft to reflect a more executive-friendly position while keeping the tone commercial and non-adversarial. I did not disclose the client’s confidential ceiling. I tightened compensation, expanded severance, and narrowed the non-compete to improve enforceability and reduce post-employment restraint. I also noted that benefit and severance details should be completed in exhibits or a schedule so the agreement can move quickly.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thanks for the first draft. We’ve marked up a streamlined executive-friendly version that keeps the deal moving while tightening the economics and narrowing the post-employment restrictions. In short: base compensation should be fixed in an exhibit, severance should be more clearly defined and triggered by a broader set of qualifying terminations, and the non-compete should be narrowed in scope, geography, and duration, with customary carveouts. Happy to discuss any open business points live so we can get this finalized quickly.

edits.text: 3. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive a base salary, target bonus opportunity, and customary employee benefits as set forth in Exhibit A, subject to annual review and adjustment in the sole discretion of the Board acting in good faith. The Company shall reimburse reasonable business expenses incurred in the performance of duties in accordance with Company policy.
edits.name: compensation

edits.text: 4. SEVERANCE. Upon a termination of employment by the Company without Cause or by the Executive for Good Reason, the Executive shall be entitled to the severance benefits set forth in Exhibit B, subject to execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims. Severance shall include continued base salary for a stated period, any earned but unpaid bonus, accrued vacation, and continued health coverage to the extent required or permitted by law. If a termination occurs in connection with a Change in Control, the Executive shall receive the enhanced severance, if any, specified in Exhibit B.
edits.name: severance

edits.text: 5. NON-COMPETE. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the Executive shall not, for a period of six months following termination, directly engage in a substantially similar competitive business in the geographic area in which the Executive materially performed services for the Company during the twelve months preceding termination; provided, however, that nothing in this Section shall prohibit passive ownership of less than 5% of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company, general employment in a role that does not involve competitive activities, or compliance with legal, fiduciary, or whistleblower obligations. The parties acknowledge that this restriction is intended to be narrowly tailored to protect legitimate business interests.
edits.name: non-compete
